Squads:

Riley Meredith to Harry Brook, no run, angled in, length delivery, Harry Brook jumped down like a cat on a hot tin roof and got beaten on the inside edge. The bowler heard something and convinced his skipper to take the review. The UltraEdge made it clear as there was nothing on it

Riley Meredith to Harry Brook, FOUR, that's a Brook wristy shovelled sliced educated edge. Didn't get the right words to pen that shot down. Moved away, was a fuller length delivery, Harry Brook stayed inside the line of the delivery and almost shovelled it off the outer-half of the bat to send it wide of the man at short third man. Full of risk but useful for now

Riley Meredith to Harry Brook, no run, banged in short, Harry Brook lets his bat hanging and the ball goes off the shoulder of the bat and lands short of the man at mid-wicket. Harry Brook was ball watching and didn't intend to take the run
Riley Meredith to Harry Brook, wide, banged in short, Harry Brook was backing away and has been wided
Riley Meredith to Harry Brook, no run, moves across, length delivery and Harry Brook looks to scoop it but misses
Riley Meredith to Harry Brook, 2 runs, fuller length delivery, driven down to long-on for a brace. The batter backed away and played it down the ground. The long-on was a little square
Ben Dwarshuis [1.0-0-11-0] is back into the attack
Ben Dwarshuis to Phil Salt, THATS OUT!! Caught&Bowled!!

Ben Dwarshuis to Phil Salt, out Caught&Bowled!! Is that Spiderman? Or is it super glue which has helped. That was a back of a length delivery, Philip Salt swatted it back and the bowler flung his right hand out to take it. The batter stood tall and wanted to tonk that back past the bowler and was to the wrong side of the bowler who is a southpaw but Ben Dwarshuis did well. Reflex catch and Aussies can delay the formalities for a while now. Phil Salt c and b Ben Dwarshuis 58(30) [4s-5 6s-4]
Tom Banton, right handed bat, comes to the crease
Ben Dwarshuis to Tom Banton, 1 run, stands tall and punches the ball down to mid-off for a single
Ben Dwarshuis to Harry Brook, 1 run, short ball, angled in, pulled down to fine leg for a single

Ben Dwarshuis to Tom Banton, FOUR, Tom Banton puts his name in the list of marauders for the day. That was short, outside off, angled across, Tom Banton got hold of it and pulled it over mid-wicket. That was thwacked
Ben Dwarshuis to Tom Banton, 1 run, on a length, angled across, tucked down to deep mid for a single. Closed the face of the bat
Ben Dwarshuis to Harry Brook, 1 run, backs away to a short ball and pulls the ball down to deep mid for a single

Adam Zampa to Harry Brook, 1 run, tucks the ball down to deep mid for a single as that was on the pads

Adam Zampa to Tom Banton, SIX, aerial ball, high ball, long ball, you know the rest of it. Tom Banton does a ballet, gets to the pitch of the ball and launches it over long-on. For a second it looked like, he was done in by the flight but kept his balance to send it over long-on
Adam Zampa to Tom Banton, 1 run, stabs the ball down into the off-side for a single as that one didn't spin much outside off
